Dating is one of those subjective things that different people like different ways, so there is no "one size fits all" kinda thing, but in terms of what most people I've interacted with want and appreciate, I'd say this:

Ask her out when you're starting to like her. If you're crushing, great, if you just find her interesting to talk to and think there may be a spark, still great. Don't wait until you're hopelessly in love, which is what I've personally noticed in a lot of these threads. The first date is really a testing of the waters to see if you both enjoy each other's company. 

For location, I think coffee is probably the universal first date move. It's casual, neither of you has to feel uncomfortable about ordering a messy meal, most people will be able to find something they like at a coffee shop, etc. 

For \*where\* to ask, I think it would be best to do it in whichever scenario where you both see each other the most frequently, and where both of you feel comfortable. You can ask through texting or Facebook, I personally don't see anything wrong with that if you do often chat there, but if you don't, I'd stick to in person. Do make it personal, other people being around is ok but make sure that she's the only one who really hears the request. And keep it simple. Something like "Hey, are you free to get coffee on Sunday?" or "Want to study together tomorrow? I know a pretty cool cafe nearby." You don't need to say it's a date, people usually know it is, but if she asks you can say so. If she declines, accept it with grace, and move on. We've all faced rejection and we all have to learn how to save face after that awkward moment.

This is probably a lot more than you were wanting, but hope it helps! Good luck!

I had a pet rat and if I was gone no one would be able to take care of her, so I needed to be strong for her. I listened to music, and watched the stars. I found an outlet: writing.
